comments.body:
I found that `IsTopKIndexOutputUsed`, introduced in #43952, misses cases where the TopK tuple or its extracted indices are returned directly as the computation result. These outputs remain observable even when they have no instruction users.

I opened #49006 to handle both cases while preserving the values-only optimization for genuinely unused indices. The new HLO regression tests failed before the change and passed with the fix.

issue.body:
On TPU v4-8 devices, `jax.lax.top_k` produces an incorrect local output shape for indices when the results are returned directly from a batch-sharded computation.

For an input of shape `[32,4096]` and `k=50`, the input and both outputs use `P("d", None)` on a mesh with `d=4`. Both local outputs should therefore have shape `[8,50]`. Instead, the optimized executable declares values as `f32[8,50]` and indices as `s32[32,50]`, and `jax.device_get` fails.

Adding an arithmetic operation on the indices before returning them makes host materialization succeed with the expected shapes. This appears related to the index-use predicate introduced in [#43952](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/43952).

## Environment

- Python 3.12
- JAX 0.11.1
- jaxlib 0.11.1
- libtpu 0.0.46
- TPU v4-8
- Input dtype: `float32`


## Minimal reproducer

```python
import importlib.metadata as metadata

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
from jax.sharding import Mesh, NamedSharding
from jax.sharding import PartitionSpec as P

print({
    "jax": jax.__version__,
    "jaxlib": metadata.version("jaxlib"),
    "libtpu": metadata.version("libtpu"),
    "devices": [str(device) for device in jax.devices()],
})
assert jax.device_count() == 4

mesh = Mesh(np.asarray(jax.devices()), ("d",))
rows = NamedSharding(mesh, P("d", None))

input_x = jnp.arange(32 * 4096, dtype=jnp.float32).reshape(32, 4096)
x = jax.device_put(input_x, rows)
top_k = jax.jit(
    lambda value: tuple(jax.lax.top_k(value, 50)),
    in_shardings=rows,
    out_shardings=(rows, rows),
)
compiled = top_k.lower(x).compile()
print((compiled.as_text() or "").splitlines()[0])
values, indices = jax.device_get(compiled(x))
print(values.shape, indices.shape)
```
Run with:

```bash
JAX_PLATFORMS=tpu,cpu python repro.py
```

The failing run reports:

```text
ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (32,50) into shape (8,50)
```

The relevant part of the optimized HLO header, reformatted for readability, is:

```text
entry_computation_layout={
  (f32[8,4096]{1,0:T(8,128)})->
  (f32[8,50]{1,0:T(8,128)}, s32[32,50]{1,0:T(8,128)})
}
num_partitions=4
```


## Expected behavior

Both local outputs should have shape `[8,50]`, and both arrays should materialize on the host with global shape `[32,50]`.

The original sweep tested `V=1024,1536,2048,3072,4096`. The first four sizes materialized successfully with the expected shapes; `4096` is the smallest failing size tested, not an established exact threshold.

## Additional comparisons

The following return forms were tested at `V=4096`, using the same environment, input sharding, and batch sharding for each returned array. Single-array returns use `out_shardings=rows`; two-array returns use `out_shardings=(rows, rows)`.

| Return expression after `values, indices = jax.lax.top_k(x, 50)` | Optimized local output shapes | Host materialization |
|---|---|---|
| `(values, indices)` | `(f32[8,50], s32[32,50])` | Fails |
| `indices` | `s32[32,50]` | Fails |
| `(values, indices + jnp.arange(50))` | `(f32[8,50], s32[8,50])` | Succeeds |
| `values` | `f32[8,50]` | Succeeds |

Returning only `indices` also reproduces the same local-shape mismatch and `jax.device_get` error. Returning only `values` succeeds.
issue.title: [SPMD] TopK produces incorrect local index shapes when returned directly

issue.body:
📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #49005.

Fix `IsTopKIndexOutputUsed` so that returning either the complete TopK `(values, indices)` tuple or just its `indices` element as the computation result counts as using the indices.

The check now recognizes a root TopK custom call and uses `!IsDead()` for the `get-tuple-element` instruction that extracts the indices. This preserves the values-only optimization for truly unused indices.

🎯 Justification

A computation root is observable by its caller even when its instruction-user list is empty. Checking only instruction users misses these root uses and selects the values-only path, which substitutes a dummy index tensor with the global `{batch_size, k}` shape.

For batch-sharded TopK, can produces a global-sized index output where a partition-local shape is required. The JAX reproducer observes `f32[8,50]` values and `s32[32,50]` indices on four TPU v4 devices, causing `jax.device_get` to fail.

This change restores their correct partition-local shape, as verified by the HLO regression tests.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

🧪 Unit Tests:

Added:

- `TopKCustomCallTupleRootUsesIndices`
- `TopKCustomCallIndexRootUsesIndices`

Both tests shard a batch of 64 rows across two devices. They fail with the implementation change removed and pass with the fix:

| HLO root case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| TopK tuple root | `(bf16[32,40], s32[64,40])` | `(bf16[32,40], s32[32,40])` |
| Index get-tuple-element root | `s32[64,40]` | `s32[32,40]` |

The following local test runs passed:

```bash
bazel test //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test \
  --test_filter='*TopKCustomCall*RootUsesIndices*'

bazel test //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test \
  --test_filter='*TopKCustomCall*'

bazel test //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test
```

The full test target passed all 10 shards, including the existing values-only TopK coverage. Formatting checks with clang-format 17.0.6 and `git diff --check` also passed.

PR #49006: Fix SPMD TopK root index outputs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49006

📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #49005.

Fix `IsTopKIndexOutputUsed` so that returning either the complete TopK `(values, indices)` tuple or just its `indices` element as the computation result counts as using the indices.

The check now recognizes a root TopK custom call and uses `!IsDead()` for the `get-tuple-element` instruction that extracts the indices. This preserves the values-only optimization for truly unused indices.

🎯 Justification

A computation root is observable by its caller even when its instruction-user list is empty. Checking only instruction users misses these root uses and selects the values-only path, which substitutes a dummy index tensor with the global `{batch_size, k}` shape.

For batch-sharded TopK, can produces a global-sized index output where a partition-local shape is required. The JAX reproducer observes `f32[8,50]` values and `s32[32,50]` indices on four TPU v4 devices, causing `jax.device_get` to fail.

This change restores their correct partition-local shape, as verified by the HLO regression tests.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

🧪 Unit Tests:

Added:

- `TopKCustomCallTupleRootUsesIndices`
- `TopKCustomCallIndexRootUsesIndices`

Both tests shard a batch of 64 rows across two devices. They fail with the implementation change removed and pass with the fix:

| HLO root case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| TopK tuple root | `(bf16[32,40], s32[64,40])` | `(bf16[32,40], s32[32,40])` |
| Index get-tuple-element root | `s32[64,40]` | `s32[32,40]` |

The following local test runs passed:

```bash
bazel test //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test \
  --test_filter='*TopKCustomCall*RootUsesIndices*'

bazel test //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test \
  --test_filter='*TopKCustomCall*'

bazel test //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test
```

The full test target passed all 10 shards, including the existing values-only TopK coverage. Formatting checks with clang-format 17.0.6 and `git diff --check` also passed.
